title: Discord Music Bot — Service Overview
description: Traces, logs, span-derived metrics, Redis, and container metrics for the music bot. Provisioned from grafana/dashboards/json/ — read-only in the UI; edit the JSON (see docs/GRAFANA_DASHBOARD_PLAN.md).

panels.title: Commands / min
panels.description: All command.<name> spans (Tempo span-metrics). One per prefix command invocation.

panels.title: Command error rate
panels.description: Share of command spans ending STATUS_CODE_ERROR (set by _report_command_error / cog_command_error).

panels.title: Command p95 latency
panels.description: p95 across all commands. -play resolves metadata inline, so it dominates the tail.

panels.title: Songs played
panels.description: player.loop.iteration spans over the dashboard range — one per song the playback loop processed (including failed streams).

panels.title: Errors logged
panels.description: ERROR-severity log records over the dashboard range (Loki). Includes command failures, playback errors, drainer alarms.

panels.title: Redis memory used
panels.description: redis-server used_memory as a share of maxmemory (256 MB in compose), from the otelcol-metrics sidecar — its redis receiver enables the opt-in redis.maxmemory metric, so this ratio tracks whatever cap the server actually runs with; no hardcoded threshold to drift. history:outbox and guild:*:history are non-evictable — sustained growth here is the push_history ISSUE marker in redis_client.py.

panels.title: Command rate
panels.description: Per-command invocation rate from command.<name> spans.

panels.title: Command p95 duration
panels.description: Per-command p95 from the span-metrics latency histogram. Exemplars link straight to Tempo traces.

panels.title: Command errors
panels.description: Commands whose span ended in error status. Every one carries a trace: the user-facing embed footer holds the trace id.

panels.title: Command errors (logged, by command)
panels.description: The "<command> failed:" funnel in _report_command_error, grouped by the structlog `command` contextvar (bound in cog_before_invoke).

targets.expr: sum by (command) (count_over_time({service_name="discord-music-bot", deployment_environment=~"$environment"} | json | level="error" | command != `` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Songs played
panels.description: Playback-loop iterations per hour — one per song dequeued and played (span closes at song end, so a 4-minute song lands ~4 minutes after it started).

panels.title: Extraction latency p95 (yt-dlp phases)
panels.description: ytdl.yt_source (phase 1 resolve), ytdl.prefetch_stream / ytdl.yt_stream (phase 2/3 stream extraction), ytdl.yt_playlist. Cache hits keep these near zero; a jump means yt-dlp is doing real network rounds again.

panels.title: Stream failures
panels.description: The three distinct failure surfaces of the playback loop (musicplayer.py). Dead streams also invalidate the cached URL and re-extract.

panels.title: yt-dlp health signals
panels.description: yt-dlp's own warning channel (SABR / PO-token / signature messages — the early-warning system for YouTube rule changes), URL revocations, and ProcessPool breakage.

panels.title: Serving-format degradation (fires once per format per process)
panels.description: _record_serving_format warns when songs degrade to muxed/HLS formats — the observable symptom of the android_vr primary path being down. Deduped per format_id per process: judge by PRESENCE in the window, never by rate.

panels.title: Outbox drain cycles
panels.description: history.drain spans from HistoryOutboxDrainer._drain_once. Span attributes carry drain.batch / drain.parsed / drain.tombstones / drain.rejected per cycle.

panels.title: Outbox data-loss & backlog alarms
panels.description: Anything non-zero here is real data loss or a drain stall — see the outbox section of redis_client.py and `just outbox`. Tombstones and cap drops are unrecoverable.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="discord-music-bot", deployment_environment=~"$environment"} |= `whose payload had already been deleted` [$__auto]))

panels.title: Redis write pressure
panels.description: @_guild_op swallows Redis errors and returns defaults — the bot keeps working degraded, so THIS is the only place those failures are visible. maxmemory refusals on the history key mean plays are about to be lost.

panels.title: Client operation rate (Redis commands + outbound HTTP)
panels.description: Auto-instrumented client spans. UPPERCASE names are Redis commands (HGETALL, LPUSH, XADD…); GET/POST also covers aiohttp calls to YouTube/Spotify/Discord CDNs — the two overlap on GET/SET (span metrics carry no db.system label).

panels.title: Client operation p95
panels.description: Redis ops should sit in the low milliseconds; HTTP extraction calls in the hundreds of ms. The playback loop never awaits Postgres, so no asyncpg spans exist by design.

panels.title: Redis memory
panels.description: From the otelcol-metrics sidecar's redis receiver (the opt-in redis.maxmemory metric is enabled in grafana/otelcol-metrics.yaml). maxmemory is 256 MB in compose; volatile-lru must never evict history:outbox or guild:*:history (they carry no TTL).

panels.title: Redis throughput
panels.description: Server-side command throughput and connected clients (sidecar redis receiver).

panels.title: Redis keyspace hit ratio
panels.description: ytdl:source / ytdl:stream / spotify:* cache effectiveness at the server level. Repeat plays should keep this high.

panels.title: Redis evictions
panels.description: volatile-lru evictions. TTL'd cache keys are legitimate victims under pressure, but sustained eviction while memory sits at maxmemory is the prelude to the push_history OOM failure mode.

panels.title: CPU by container
panels.description: Per-container CPU. yt-dlp extraction bursts show on the bot (its 4 pool workers live in the same container).

panels.title: Memory by container
panels.description: Per-container RSS-ish usage. The bot idles ~150 MB and grows ~80–120 MB per active yt-dlp pool worker.

panels.title: Network I/O by container
panels.description: Audio streaming is the dominant flow: CDN ingress on the bot, Opus egress to Discord voice. NOTE: the bot runs with network_mode: host, so Docker may report empty network stats for it — the redis/postgres/sidecar containers are the reliable series here.

panels.title: Block I/O by container
panels.description: Redis AOF fsync (everysec) and Postgres WAL are the expected writers.

panels.title: Log volume by level
panels.description: All log records by severity. structlog renders JSON bodies; severity rides OTLP metadata, so this counts guild_state's plain-stdlib lines too.

panels.title: Exceptions — live feed
panels.description: Errors plus any line that carried a traceback: structlog's ExceptionRenderer writes exc_info tracebacks to the `exception` field, so exc_info WARNINGs (e.g. "Failed to update bot activity") surface here too. Every line carries logger + environment, and trace_id when inside a span — the derived field links straight to the Tempo trace. Requires the JSON body, so guild_state's plain-stdlib lines are excluded (they never carry tracebacks).

panels.title: Bot logs — live feed
panels.description: Everything the bot logs, all levels, newest first, updating at the dashboard refresh cadence (30s here). For true push-streaming tail of the same query use Explore → Live.

panels.title: Slow traces (> 2 s)
panels.description: Command and pipeline traces above 2 s. player.loop.iteration spans intentionally live as long as the song they play — ignore those; look for slow command.play / ytdl.* chains.

panels.title: Errored traces
panels.description: Traces containing an error-status span. Error embeds shown to users carry `trace: <id>` in the footer — paste it into Explore to join a report to its trace.

panels.title: Collector ingest
panels.description: Spans / log records / metric points accepted by the otel-lgtm collector (its self-scrape). A flatline while the bot is up means telemetry is silently not arriving.

panels.title: Collector refusals & export failures
panels.description: Non-zero means telemetry is being dropped between the bot and Tempo/Loki/Prometheus — the dashboards lie while this is elevated.
